8.1.title: Spokane
guide_refs: Night Driving: Headlight Range and Speed

8.1.0.text: Two hours. The last two. I-90 east out of Ritzville, the sky gone from gray to black, and somewhere past the horizon a city that kept some of its lights on.

8.1.lights_a.speaker: ALI
8.1.lights_a.text: Lights. Shadow inside the light. Hold it there. Two hours.

8.1.lights_b.speaker: ALI
8.1.lights_b.text: Old lights. Slower, then. …Sori was worth it.

8.1.retry.speaker: ALI
8.1.retry.text: Long way around. Both cats. Same city. Fewer mistakes.

8.1.city.text: The Division exit. Sprague Avenue. Stop signs, a school with its lights still going, tracks, a four-way — everything from Kent, in a different order, and none of it new.

8.1.5.speaker: ALI
8.1.5.text: …They didn't even look. Tuna, I love you.

8.1.5r.speaker: ALI
8.1.5r.text: …They didn't even look. Ritzville guy, I love you. Tuna, I love you more.

8.1.speed_ok.text: Twenty-five. Exactly. Two figures behind the sawhorses, closer every second, and the speedometer doesn't move.

8.1.speed_ok2.speaker: ALI
8.1.speed_ok2.text: Don't rush the last two hours.

8.1.8.speaker: ALI
8.1.8.text: Okay. Parallel park. Fred Meyer lot. Forty times. One more.

8.1.curb.text: Curb. Behind the sawhorses, a hand goes to a mouth. Nobody else hears it.

8.1.over_line.text: Over the line. Six inches of paint under the bumper.

8.1.gap_foot.text: The front bumper stops a foot from the line. Maybe less. No squeal.

8.1.gap_ok.text: A little over a foot from the line. No squeal. Nobody's measuring. Ali is.

8.1.gap_far.text: Not a foot. Not close. But straight, and quiet, and here.

8.1.swarm.speaker: MOM
8.1.swarm.text: Ali? Dispatch has movement on Sprague. Is that — are you —

8.1.swarm2.speaker: ALI
8.1.swarm2.text: I'm fine. Both cats. Coming around the long way.

8.2.pre.text: Division Street. The checkpoint gate. Two figures behind the sawhorses. The Beetle rolls the last fifty feet at exactly the posted speed.

8.2.pre_b.text: Division Street. The checkpoint gate. Two figures behind the sawhorses. The Beetle rolls the last fifty feet slower than the posted speed — she caught it.

8.2.stop_foot.text: It stops with the front bumper a foot from the line. No squeal.

8.2.stop_close.text: It stops with the front bumper a little over a foot from the line. No squeal.

8.2.stop_far.text: It stops. Not close to the line. No squeal. Nobody behind the sawhorses is looking at the line.

8.2.out.text: Ali gets out. Mya is asleep in the passenger seat. Gracie is on the dashboard, yelling silently through the glass.

8.2.walk.text: Mom doesn't run — nobody runs anymore. She walks fast, very quiet, and holds on.

8.2.4.text: Ray, behind her, holding the gray blanket. Looking at the car.

8.2.7.text: Ray, for a moment, has nothing.

8.2.8.speaker: RAY
8.2.8.text: We're going to need to talk about insurance.

8.2.10b.speaker: RAY
8.2.10b.text: Did you check the tire pressure?

8.2.12b.speaker: RAY
8.2.12b.text: …Most is good. Most is honest. We'll do the rest tomorrow.

8.2.lights1.speaker: MOM
8.2.lights1.text: You came in with the old lights. In the dark.

8.2.stall_a1.speaker: ALI
8.2.stall_a1.text: {RAY}. A kid named Jonah says thank you.

8.2.stall_a3.speaker: ALI
8.2.stall_a3.text: Your truck. Breaking constantly. I knew how to hook a strap.

8.2.stall_a4.speaker: RAY
8.2.stall_a4.text: …That's the nicest thing anyone's ever said about that truck.

8.2.stall_b1.speaker: ALI
8.2.stall_b1.text: …Somebody walked six hours because of me, once. He says it was the right call.

8.2.stall_b7.speaker: MOM
8.2.stall_b7.text: Okay. You're home. That's the whole answer tonight.

8.2.13.text: He puts the gray blanket over the roof of the Beetle. Gracie immediately attacks it.

8.2.14.text: Mya does not wake up. She has not woken up for anything that mattered less than this, and she isn't starting now.

8.3.0.text: A week later. The Spokane Relay. A headset that isn't hers, a chair that is now. Two cats on a gray blanket in the corner. Ali keys the mic.

8.3.1.speaker: ALI
8.3.1.text: Spokane Relay to Kent Valley. Deac, if you're on —

8.3.2.speaker: ALI
8.3.2.text: I got here. Both cats. Permit's on the fridge. {MOM} put a magnet on it. A cat magnet. It's very embarrassing.

8.3.3.speaker: ALI
8.3.3.text: Tell Jonah he still drives like a golf cart.

8.3.3b.speaker: ALI
8.3.3b.text: Tell him {RAY} says you're welcome. He'll know.

8.3.4.speaker: ALI
8.3.4.text: Tell Bea I'm getting a third cat and it's her fault.

8.3.4b.speaker: ALI
8.3.4b.text: Tell her the mouse made it. Tell her she was right about the bridge. She'll be insufferable. Tell her anyway.

8.3.5.speaker: ALI
8.3.5.text: Tell Tuna {RAY} wants to know what gauge the doors are and I told him it's a filing cabinet and he didn't believe me.

8.3.5b.speaker: ALI
8.3.5b.text: Tell him the muffler's the reason nobody in Spokane looked up. He knows. Tell him anyway.

8.3.6.speaker: ALI
8.3.6.text: Tell Priya HUSH played "Hold Still" last night and the whole Relay sang it. Under their breath. Fifty people. Priya was right. I'd never heard anything like it.

8.3.6b.speaker: ALI
8.3.6b.text: Tell her Sori's on the visor. Tell her I didn't tell Jonah.

8.3.hank.speaker: ALI
8.3.hank.text: Tell Hank — no. Hank's not yours. If you see him anyway, tell him I didn't do anything stupid on the way in either.

8.3.7.text: Pause. The Relay hums. Gracie rearranges the blanket.

8.3.13.text: Ali, in a chair that is now hers, puts her hand flat on the desk and doesn't say anything for a while.

8.3.silence.text: Static. Only static. The mountains eat radio, and the pass is a long way from here.
